answer: Mutual-information collapse. Canary probes wander far from memorizable text; each response stream is compressed. If two streams compress better jointly than apart they share one generator: the pair links and its whole component is capped at one share and loses its attestations. So a thousand ivory keys buy nothing - keys are free, but every clone on one model emits the same vine of outputs and links to each sibling. The test is pairwise, so N heads face N^2 comparisons, and collapse spreads by component: one link sinks the cluster. Attacker cost: N independent generators, not N keys.
